evidence.text_excerpt: > The bell gives a thin jingle, like it’s apologizing for existing. The air inside is **dry** — paper, hemp, metal, and the sharp sweet of cheap dye cakes. Shelves climb to the ceiling on runner’s legs; a ladder on wheels blocks one aisle like it’s guarding a fortress. Behind the counter, bolts of cloth lean like tired soldiers. Someone has pinned a **charms-against-mice** above the scale: not magic, just superstition and confidence.

evidence.text_excerpt: > You made camp in the shadow of a storm that **shimmers**. Lysandra is with you again — awake, fragile, furious at the gaps in her own memory. Supplies are being **burned** down to what you can trust. Caelynn’s rockie-talkie is still trying to turn **Mirathorn’s silence** into an answer. Mossford thinks you’ve gone; Ephanna, you’re the one who said you’re going **back** — under a different face — before the rain makes liars of all of you.

> Mossford is behind you — still cheering, still digging in, still wondering what it means that the forest **turned away** instead of swallowing them. Out here, the world feels bigger and less impressed by your victory. > > The camp is **real work**: lines tightened, canvas snapping in a wind that has opinions, animals complaining in that honest way that means they’re scared of the sky. **Karesmine** keeps glancing **northeast**, where the mass is still assembling — a system **riding southwest** like something driven by a hand on a map. It doesn’t look like weather you outlast by ignoring it — the clouds have a **shimmer** in them, like heat… or like something **remembered wrong**. > > **Lys

**Lysandra** is **with the party again**, physically found at a **half-unpacked wagon** in the wild. She was **under cult-tinted influence** (shimmer eyes); **Caelynn’s tea** broke the surface of it. Lysandra remembers **voices in the dark** after the party entered the forest, **gaps in time**, **meat-smell** while trying to sleep — and she had been **drawing** something she called a **tower** and “where the voices are.” That drawing is still **player knowledge** as a lead, not necessarily literal truth.

The **forest crisis at Mossford is resolved** in the town’s favor: the ditch-fires worked; the trees **withdrew and turned east**. The Questionable Company got their public thank-you — and then **named their own departure**, cutting off Marla’s ask for justice on Bonogo before it could become a town trial.

The experience that I want to set up for and I hoep to execute on or generally put in front of the players is to start rapidly upping the pressure. Working to drive them forward at a reckless rate. I want them to have to question whether they can do more "good" or "impact" by staying where they are and helping or if the most effective action is to press on towards the swamp, to try an work out what this drawing Lysandra made is, to get to the swamp.

At this point in my imagination what was once the swamp community has become not a tower as they interpreted the map but a fleshy lovecraftian hole in the ground that becomes a dimension and mind bending trip to somewhere else that is not fun. I want the players to get there, see the hole this maddening maze into a dirt hole, that shows signs of becoming some kind of living corrupted meat thing. To ask where did all this meat come from and not like the answer.

Lets start with an brainstorming idea dump, not everything here works, this is just ideas. I don't want model assistance here, I want to have my unrefined prose stored and flagged as brainstorming.  This is prep for Longmont Campaign 2 Session 21
